title: Point dualizing identification is compatible with coefficient change
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] at a coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, and put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, with constructibility and finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $c=F_\Lambda C$, $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let
$$j_{\Lambda,C}:F_\Lambda(D_sC)\xrightarrow{\sim}c^\vee$$
be the specified identification of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], where $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)$. Let $Q$ be finite reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ ($1\leq m\leq n$), integral reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, integral scalar extension for a finite coefficient-field extension, rationalization, or extension at a common finite field stage. On point sheaves use the stipulated coefficient functor $Q_s$ and on coefficient modules use $q$. Write
$$t_{Q,B}:q(F_\Lambda B)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\Lambda'}(Q_sB)$$
for the canonical sections/coefficient comparison, natural in $B\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$: for $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$ it is the sections/derived-reduction isomorphism of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction]; for integral scalar extension and for extension at a common finite field stage it is the inverse of the sections scalar-extension isomorphism $\varphi$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] (rationalized in the latter case); for rationalization it is the identity, $F_E$ being $\Gamma(s,-)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; for $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ it is the map $\Gamma(s,B)\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}\to\Gamma(s,B\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m})$ induced by tensoring sections, whose invertibility on $D^b_{ctf}(s,A_{E,n})$ is part of the present assertion. Its compatibility with the unit and tensor constraints is that of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Let $\delta_{Q,C}:Q_s(D_sC)\to D_s(Q_sC)$ be the canonical internal-Hom comparison using the identity-adjunction coefficient comparison $Q_s\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\omega_{s,\Lambda'}$, and let $b_{Q,c}:q(c^\vee)\to(qc)^\vee$ be the canonical derived module-dual comparison. The site comparisons are those of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] on its domains and the finite-Tor comparisons of [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Then
$$t_{Q,C}^{\vee}\circ j_{\Lambda',Q_sC}\circ F_{\Lambda'}(\delta_{Q,C})\circ t_{Q,D_sC}
=b_{Q,c}\circ q(j_{\Lambda,C}).$$
Both sides are morphisms from $q(F_\Lambda D_sC)$ to $(qc)^\vee$; $t_{Q,C}^{\vee}$ is precomposition by $t_{Q,C}$.

proof.text: First identify sections with the inverse image of a ringed topos point, at finite coefficients. In [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point] take the geometric point $\operatorname{id}_s$ of $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The pointed-neighbourhood category has initial object $(s,\operatorname{id}_s)$: its map to $(U,u)$ is precisely the specified lift $u:s\to U$. Its opposite therefore has terminal object $(s,\operatorname{id}_s)$, so the stalk colimit is $\mathcal F(s)$. Thus $p^{-1}=\Gamma(s,-)$. For $A=A_{E,n}$ and any constant $A$-module $M$, [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] identifies $\Gamma(s,\underline M)=M$ through the constant-section map. Give $p$ the ring map $p^{-1}A_s=A\xrightarrow{1}A$. Its module pullback is $A\otimes_A\Gamma(s,-)=\Gamma(s,-)$, which is exact on the entire ambient module category by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to this ringed point. On a K-flat flat-term resolution its comparison is termwise sections; exactness from step 1 identifies $Lp^*$ with ambient derived sections. Now use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] with $G=(A_{E,m})_s$, regarded as an $A_{E,n}$-module. It gives, for $1\leq m\leq n$ and any ambient complex $B$,
$$\Gamma(s,B\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}(A_{E,m})_s)\cong\Gamma(s,B)\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}.$$
The inverse is exactly $t_{Q,B}$: the tensor-pullback map on resolutions is the balanced map induced by tensoring sections, and the identification of $\Gamma(s,(A_{E,m})_s)$ is the constant-section map of step 1. This proves the missing invertibility assertion, including for $B=C,D_sC$ once their domains are checked below. The theorem applies on unbounded ambient categories, so no finite-Tor hypothesis on $A_{E,m}$ over $A_{E,n}$ is needed; such a hypothesis would be false when $m<n$.

proof.text: For integral reduction, [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] gives the stipulated $t_{Q,B}$ as an isomorphism. For integral scalar extension, [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] gives $t_{Q,B}=\varphi^{-1}$, explicitly the canonical sections-tensor map followed by the completion comparison, and gives its rationalized version at a common coefficient field. For rationalization the two fibre functors give the same module complex by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], so $t$ is the identity. Use [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] for the fibre tensor isomorphisms, their unit constraints, and their compatibility with these coefficient maps. In particular the comparisons used here are the actual specified maps, with $\varphi$ inverted in the stated direction, rather than unspecified objectwise isomorphisms.

proof.text: The domains required in steps 2--3 hold. The isomorphism $u_\Lambda:\omega_{s,\Lambda}\to\Lambda_s$ is the identity-adjunction normalization of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. Hence $D_sC$ is internal Hom of $C$ into the coefficient unit. The unit has Tor interval $[0,0]$ by the definition [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For the finite stage, apply (ii) and (vii) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] to $X=s$, and its integral and field-stage assertions to the other stages. They put $D_sC$, $Q_sC$ and $D_s(Q_sC)$ in the required bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. The evaluation compatibility in (vii), with [lem-fix-operation-reduction] on its stated domains, applies to the canonical internal-Hom arrow $\delta_{Q,C}$. We do not infer that arbitrary constructible finite-Tor sheaves on a positive-dimensional scheme are site-perfect, nor use the site-perfect formula outside its domain.

source.place: second paragraph: site-perfect coefficient compatibility at the point

proof.text:
Fix notation for evaluation and the canonical identifications. Put $d=F_\Lambda(D_sC)$, and let $\mu_\Lambda:d\otimes^L c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\Lambda(D_sC\otimes^L C)$ be the inverse tensor comparison of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Let $e_\Lambda:d\otimes^Lc\to\Lambda$ be $F_\Lambda(u_\Lambda\circ\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\mu_\Lambda$, with the fibre unit identified with $\Lambda$. Unpack the specified canonical internal-Hom identification $j_{\Lambda,C}$ of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]: its map into the coefficient Hom is the tensor--Hom transpose of evaluation after sections, followed by $u_\Lambda$. Thus
$$\operatorname{ev}_c\circ(j_{\Lambda,C}\otimes1_c)=e_\Lambda.$$
This is the defining adjunct identity, not an extra isomorphism theorem. On Hom-complex representatives [def-pur-hom-complex] it says that a degree-$r$ family $f$ acts on a section $x$ by $u_\Lambda(f(x))$; the differential on both sides is $d f-(-1)^r f d$. The same description defines $j$ after rationalization and at a common field stage. Use the symmetry constraint if evaluation is written with the input first. The adjunction inverse identities of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] give precisely the displayed identity, and give the corresponding identity for $j_{\Lambda',Q_sC}$.

source.place: second paragraph: site-perfect coefficient compatibility at the point

proof.text:
Write $\nu_q:qd\otimes^L qc\xrightarrow{\sim}q(d\otimes^Lc)$ for the scalar-extension tensor constraint and put $E=q(e_\Lambda)\circ\nu_q$, with $q\Lambda=\Lambda'$. Let $e' = e_{\Lambda'}$ be the pairing of step 5 for $Q_sC$. The definition of the canonical internal-Hom comparison $\delta_{Q,C}$ as the transpose of coefficient-changed evaluation gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{Q_sC}\circ(\delta_{Q,C}\otimes1)=Q_s(\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\nu_{Q_s},$$
including the stipulated comparison on the dualizing objects. After $u_{\Lambda'}$ this comparison is $Q_su_\Lambda$, since it is the identity-adjunction coefficient comparison. Apply $F_{\Lambda'}$ to this equality. Naturality of $t$ for $u_\Lambda\circ\operatorname{ev}_C$, and the tensor and unit compatibility of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], give
$$e'\circ\bigl((F_{\Lambda'}(\delta_{Q,C})\circ t_{Q,D_sC})\otimes t_{Q,C}\bigr)=E.$$
Here preservation of evaluation under coefficient change is supplied on the finite-Tor domains by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii), and at the other stated coefficient passages by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. This proves an equality of the actual pairings before taking transposes.

proof.text:
Let $L$ denote the left side of the asserted equation. Its tensor--Hom transpose is a pairing $qd\otimes^L qc\to\Lambda'$. Precomposition by $t_{Q,C}$ in the dual means that this pairing is
$$\operatorname{ev}_{F_{\Lambda'}Q_sC}\circ\bigl((j_{\Lambda',Q_sC}\circ F_{\Lambda'}\delta_{Q,C}\circ t_{Q,D_sC})\otimes t_{Q,C}\bigr).$$
By step 5 this is the left side of the last equality in step 6, hence is $E$. This uses only the evaluation formula for uncurrying and its naturality in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]; no invertibility of $\delta$ or of a dual-base-change arrow is used.

source.place: second paragraph: site-perfect coefficient compatibility at the point

proof.text:
Let $R=b_{Q,c}\circ q(j_{\Lambda,C})$. By definition the canonical module-dual comparison $b_{Q,c}$ is the transpose of coefficient-changed module evaluation. Its evaluation identity is
$$\operatorname{ev}_{qc}\circ(b_{Q,c}\otimes1_{qc})=q(\operatorname{ev}_c)\circ\nu_{q,c^\vee,c}.$$
Naturality of the tensor constraint therefore makes the transpose of $R$ equal to
$$q\bigl(\operatorname{ev}_c\circ(j_{\Lambda,C}\otimes1_c)\bigr)\circ\nu_q=q(e_\Lambda)\circ\nu_q=E,$$
by step 5. The same adjunction bijection [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] gives equal morphisms from equal transposes, so $L=R$. The calculation takes place in each stipulated coefficient category; at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it is performed at a common finite coefficient field, as prescribed in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Both sides then represent the same morphism in the common-stage category. This proves the square for every listed $Q$.

Step 1: (s,id) is the initial pointed neighbourhood, so p^{-1}=Γ(s,-); constant-sheaf-stalk gives Γ((A_m)_s)=A_m. Step 2: the ambient tensor-pullback theorem covers unbounded categories, so it applies to the quotient A_m, which has no finite Tor amplitude over A_n. I checked from that node's proof steps 5–6 that its canonical arrow is the inverse of the map that tensors sections, so it is the item's t. Restriction of scalars is conservative, so t is invertible over A_m. Step 3: the directions of t are right (φ is inverted; rationalization is the identity). Step 4: the domains follow from thm-sf-ctf-stability (ii) and (vii) at X=s and lem-fix-operation-reduction. Step 5: j is the transpose of evaluation after sections, followed by u. This matches the adjunction m↦v_s(1⊗m) and the Hom-complex signs in steps 3, 6 and 7 of lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex. Steps 6–8: I recomputed the pairing chain using the definition of δ, the fibre tensor compatibility with reduction and scalar extension, naturality of t and unit compatibility. Both transposes equal q(e)∘ν_q, and no step uses invertibility of δ or b. Edge cases checked: C=0, the unit and its shifts, m=n, A_2→A_1, L=E, rationalization and the common stage at Q̄ℓ. Minor remarks, not faults: in steps 2 and 5 the canonical arrows are identified from the cited nodes' constructions; the evaluation-preservation citations in step 6 are not needed; and lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction could serve as an alternative existence citation for step 2.
